cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Paleoanthropology ≠ Modern sociology – the branch of anthropology concerned with fossil hominids.

p.em: Example: Paleoanthropology reshapes our understanding of human origins.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hominin ≠ Non-primate – any member of the zoological group including modern humans and extinct human species.

p.em: Example: Multiple hominin species coexisted in Africa millions of years ago.

cosy-blockquote.p: Lineage ≠ Posterity – direct descent from an ancestor; ancestry or pedigree.

p.em: Example: Genetic analysis revealed a previously unknown evolutionary lineage.

cosy-blockquote.p: Genome ≠ Phenotype – the complete set of genes or genetic material present in a cell or organism.

p.em: Example: Sequencing the Neanderthal genome illuminated ancient human interbreeding.

cosy-blockquote.p: Interbreeding ≠ Reproductive isolation – breeding between different species or varieties.

p.em: Example: Interbreeding between early Homo sapiens and Neanderthals left genetic traces.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fossilized ≠ Decayed – preserved in stone or rock over geological time.

p.em: Example: Fossilized dental enamel offers chemical clues about ancient diets.

cosy-blockquote.p: Divergence ≠ Convergence – the process or state of diverging or branching off.

p.em: Example: Evolutionary divergence occurred following environmental changes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anatomy ≠ Physiology – the branch of science concerned with bodily structure.

p.em: Example: Comparative anatomy highlights structural similarities among primates.

cosy-blockquote.p: Migration ≠ Sedentary existence – movement from one region to another.

p.em: Example: Early human migration out of Africa occurred in multiple waves.

cosy-blockquote.p: Archaic ≠ Modern – very old or old-fashioned; belonging to an earlier period.

p.em: Example: Archaic human populations possessed sophisticated tool-making skills.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does ancient genome sequencing challenge traditional models of human lineage?
★ Are you fascinated by genetic history and ancestry testing?

What evidence proves that ancient hominin species engaged in frequent interbreeding?
★ What history or archaeology documentary impressed you recently?

How do fossilized remains help paleoanthropologists reconstruct prehistoric migration routes?
★ Which ancient historical site would you most like to visit?

Why is evolutionary divergence rarely a simple linear timeline?
★ How do you view the relationship between science and traditional origin stories?

What anatomical traits distinguish archaic humans from modern Homo sapiens?
★ What human physical adaptation do you find most remarkable?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
How will future discoveries in paleoanthropology alter our concept of human identity?
★ How do you think future humans will look 50,000 years from now?

Should ancient genetic data be made universally open-source for global researchers?
★ What are your thoughts on genetic privacy and open science?

How might understanding ancient migration help resolve modern cultural prejudices?
★ How can history education foster better international empathy?

Could artificial intelligence accelerate the identification of micro-fossilized fragments?
★ In what non-tech field are you most excited to see AI applied?

What ethical guidelines should govern the extraction of archaic human DNA?
★ Where should scientists set ethical limits in genetic research?
